head: claude/bybit-coverage-graded-book
title: bybit: the naked sweep must grade coverage of the book it is protecting (Tier-2, order path — DRAFT)
body:
## Tier-2, ORDER PATH — DRAFT. Do not merge without an explicit operator OK.

This changes **which live Bybit positions get a protective stop re-armed**. It is opened as a draft deliberately; auto-merge is not enabled. Precedent: #10679 sat as a draft until the operator said so.

---

## The defect

Surfaced by #10739 (merged `2c7ae605`), which deliberately did **not** fix it — correctly, because it changes re-arm behaviour and must not ride in on a diagnostic repair. Its own DONE named this as the sibling to fix next.

`_bybit_position_protection` sums **every** resting Partial SL leg on a symbol into one side-blind `covered_qty`. A protective leg is reduce-only, so it acts on the book it can **shrink** — a `Sell` reduces a LONG, a `Buy` reduces a SHORT. Under one-way netting the sum was sound: one book, so every leg was the graded book's. **Hedge mode was armed on `bybit_1`/`bybit_2` on 2026-08-30** (`BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS`), so one symbol can now carry legs for **two** books and they land in the same sum.

The consequence is in the naked sweep's re-arm decision:

```python
if covered + eps >= size: continue      # ← skips the position as "fully covered"
```

An **other-book** leg can push `covered_qty` past `size` on a position whose **own** stop is gone. The sweep then skips a genuinely naked position as fully covered, and never re-arms it.

### Evidence — and its limits

Constructed on the live `2026-09-02T03:30:33Z` reading (`/api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_1`, trader `git_sha 68e73de8`):

| | |
|---|---|
| position | `Buy 0.018 positionIdx=1` |
| its own protection | `Sell 0.018` SL + `Sell 0.018` TP — an exact 1.00× match |
| the rest | `Buy 0.46` SL + `Buy 0.46` TP, owned by **closed** trade 5308 — reduce-only orders that can only reduce a SHORT |

Had the `Sell 0.018` leg been lost, `covered` would still have read `0.46 >= 0.018` and the sweep would **not** have re-armed a naked long.

> ⚠️ **n = 1, CONSTRUCTED. No live instance of the masking has been observed.** This is a construction over a real venue reading, not a sighting. That caveat is carried verbatim into the module docstrings, the sweep docstring, the test-file header, and the backlog row below — please do not let it get upgraded downstream.

`bybit_2` (mainnet) was measured clean at `03:20Z` by the #10739 session. **No live read, cancel, or place was performed by this session** — this is a code change, not an intervention.

---

## The fix

The re-arm/top-up comparison now reads `bybit_leg_sides.graded_book_coverage(leg_side_split)` — an accessor over the split **#10739 already computes**. It is **imported, not re-derived**: two notions of "which book does this leg reduce" would be free to drift, which is the failure this repo keeps paying for.

Three sites move from the side-blind sum to the graded figure, and only these three:

1. `if graded_covered + eps >= size: continue` — the skip.
2. `partial = graded_covered > 0` — fully-naked vs partially-naked.
3. `uncovered = size - graded_covered` — the qty-scoped top-up. Sized off the side-blind sum this can go **negative** once the other book's legs exceed `size`.

Plus `_bybit_mark_fully_covered()`: the in-tick idempotency marker (a netted symbol holds many journal rows and one exchange position) had to learn about the graded figure too, or every sibling row would fire another live bracket.

### Why the trip threshold was left side-blind

**This is the whole judgement call, and it went the other way from the fix.** The side-blind sum is the **union** of two conditions — genuine same-book over-accumulation *and* other-book legs resting on the symbol. Narrowing the trip to graded-book coverage would make the other-book case **stop tripping and go silent**, which is strictly worse than the mislabelling #10739 just fixed. `covered_qty` is byte-for-byte unchanged; the over-cover page's numbers and prose are unchanged. Only the coverage/re-arm comparison moved.

---

## The four controls — both directions, or the change is decorative

All in `tests/test_bybit_naked_rearm.py` § 2026-09-02, built from the real `03:30:33Z` venue shape.

| # | Control | Test | Asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **The fix fires** | `test_naked_long_masked_by_an_other_book_leg_is_now_REARMED` | own stop gone + `Buy 0.46` other-book leg → `broker_naked == 1`, `rearmed == 1`, a real Full-mode bracket at the **journal's** levels reaches the venue. It also re-asserts `covered_qty == 0.46` against `size == 0.018` — i.e. that the masking condition is genuinely present and it is the *decision* that changed. |
| **1b** | The sharper form | `test_partial_gap_masked_by_an_other_book_leg_tops_up_the_REAL_hole` | 0.010 of its own stop survives; side-blind coverage 0.470 → old code skipped. Top-up qty is **0.008**, not `0.018 − 0.470`. |
| **2** | **The mirror** | `test_position_covered_by_its_OWN_legs_is_still_skipped` | the unaltered live shape → `broker_naked == 0`, `rearmed == 0`, `stops_set == []`. A change tested only on case 1 has been shown to fire, not to discriminate; a spurious re-arm cancels and re-places a live bracket. |
| **3** | **The union is intact** | `test_the_other_book_condition_still_TRIPS_over_cover_and_pages` | **same fixture as control 2**, so the two coexist: `over_covered == 1`, `over_cover_other_book == 1`, `over_cover_alerted == 1`, the page still says `OPPOSITE book` — while nothing is re-armed. |
| **3b** | The other arm of the union | `test_same_book_pile_up_still_trips_it_too` | a genuine same-book pile-up still trips, and is still treated as covered. |
| **4** | **We could not look** | `test_unreadable_POSITION_side_...`, `test_unreadable_LEG_side_...`, `test_ungradeable_side_does_NOT_bank_the_side_blind_sum_as_coverage` | `coverage_side_ungradeable == 1`, `rearmed == 0`, `topped_up == 0`, `stops_set == []`, and the reason token is in the log. |

Also: `test_full_mode_stop_is_unaffected_by_the_split` (a Full-mode position stop returns before the legs are read, so `covered_qty == size` is the measurement and it must **skip, not refuse** — otherwise every Full-mode position on the fleet starts reporting `coverage_side_ungradeable`), and `test_a_second_journal_row_on_the_same_symbol_does_not_rearm_twice`.

Nine more accessor controls in `tests/test_bybit_leg_sides.py`, including the mirror (`graded coverage of a SHORT is its BUY legs` — otherwise the accessor could be inverted and still pass) and the load-bearing distinction that **only-other-book-legs is a measured `0.0`, not a refusal** (returning `None` there would make the sweep refuse exactly where it must re-arm).

### Control 4 — why refusing is the safe direction, argued rather than assumed

Fail-safe is genuinely not obvious here, so: **the two available errors are not symmetric.**

- Reading an ungraded split as **not covered** drives a Full-mode re-arm. That is a **live order** which cancels the resting bracket and stamps one trade's levels over the whole netted position — and under hedge mode it would target a book we just failed to identify. It can make a correctly-protected position **worse**.
- Reading it as **covered** would be silent.
- **Refusing does neither.** It leaves whatever protection actually rests untouched, and it is **loud** — a `WARNING` naming the reason token plus its own `coverage_side_ungradeable` counter, kept separate from `unconfirmed` (the unparseable-leg-**qty** refusal) so a reader chasing one does not find the other's rows.

It is also the posture this function **already takes** for an unparseable leg qty, so it is the existing precedent rather than a new one. ⚠️ It is **not** a claim the position is protected — only that we will not act on a read we could not grade. Refusal is all-or-nothing: one ungradeable leg leaves the graded sum a **lower bound**, and a lower bound compared against `size` under-reports coverage, which drives a re-arm.

---

## What I did with #10739's pinning test

`test_covered_qty_is_still_side_blind_so_the_rearm_decision_is_unchanged` is the test written to detect exactly this change. It is **renamed and re-argued, not deleted**, and **its assertions are unchanged**:

`test_covered_qty_is_still_side_blind_because_the_TRIP_needs_the_union`

The assertions still pin `covered_qty` side-blind, which is still load-bearing — but the *reason* has inverted. It was written to guard "the order path moved when it shouldn't have"; it now guards the opposite mistake, "the trip threshold followed the order path when it shouldn't have". Its docstring quotes the old name and says why it moved, so the next reader is not left reasoning from a name that asserts something false about this system.

Same treatment for the two prose claims that became false: the `bybit_leg_sides` module docstring ("the caller's re-arm decision still reads the unchanged side-blind `covered_qty` … landing this changes no order-path behaviour") and `_bybit_position_protection`'s ("only the over-cover PAGE reads it"; "nothing about which positions get re-armed changed here"). Both are quoted, marked **must not be re-quoted**, and corrected in place — field beats comment.

## Test fixtures

Several `_FakeBybit` fixtures carried a position row with **no `side`** and legs with no `side` — a shape production does not have (a real Bybit position row always carries both; the code already logs `exchange position side unreadable` for it). They now carry `side`/`positionIdx`, extending the precedent comment **#10739 itself wrote** on the one fixture it touched. This is the pairs-`order_packages` failure shape CLAUDE.md records: tests passing against a fictional schema. The unreadable-side path is covered by the dedicated control-4 tests instead, so nothing was lost.

## What I did NOT change

- `covered_qty` — unchanged, still side-blind.
- The over-cover **trip threshold**, its page text, its numbers, its `ERROR`-not-`CRITICAL` level, its 6h durable cooldown.
- `_bybit_leg_sides.classify_leg_side` / `other_book_state` / `split_legs_by_side` — untouched; only a read-only accessor was added.
- The Alpaca and IB naked sweeps, the journal/broker divergence detector, `_attempt_naked_autoprotect`, `_bybit_top_up_partial_sl`.
- `scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py` — the offline audit keeps its own side-blind coverage. Out of scope, and named in the backlog row below.
- `config/`, `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, any `*-review-backlog.json` (a health drain is live on that file — row text is below for the manager to place).
- No collapsed-state contract registered for the accessor's four log tokens. The load-bearing distinction (*we could not grade* vs *we graded it and nothing covers this book*) is carried by `qty is None` vs `qty == 0.0`, and what **produces** it — `bybit_leg_sides.leg_side_class` — is already a declared contract. Registering a second vocabulary over the same four states would need a consumer branch per token; the caller legitimately takes **one** branch on `qty is None`, so declaring it would buy the decorative branch that guard exists to prevent. Reasoning is in the code, not just here.

## Verification

- `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` on the **committed head**: **PASS 48 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 22**. `collapsed-state-guard`, `layer-guard`, `artifact-validity-guard`, `operator-owed-guard`, `diagnostic-provenance-guard`, `provenance-consumer-guard`, `silent-empty-guard`, `env-gate-guard`, `new-table-wiring-guard` all ran and passed (none skipped). `pytest`, `import-linter` and the pinned `ruff>=0.15,<0.16` were installed rather than caveated. One earlier run failed `ruff-lint` (E702) and is fixed in its own commit; guards were re-run **after** the final code commit.
- `tests/test_bybit_naked_rearm.py` (35), `tests/test_bybit_leg_sides.py` (46), `tests/test_bybit_over_cover_naming.py` (13), `tests/test_bybit_over_cover_alert.py`, `tests/test_netting_attribution.py` — all green.
- Full-suite result is reported in a comment on this PR; CI is the authority.

---

## FOR THE MANAGER

- **This needs an explicit operator Tier-2 OK before merge.** It is an order-path change: it alters which live Bybit positions get a protective stop re-armed, on a code path shared by `bybit_1` (demo) **and `bybit_2` (mainnet)**. I hold no merge slot and have enabled no auto-merge.
- **A useful question to put to the operator alongside the approval:** should this be staged? Unlike its siblings this gate has **no `*_ACCOUNTS` allowlist** — the sweep is fleet-wide. Adding one would be a larger change and I did not make it unilaterally; the argument against is that the current behaviour can leave a real position naked, so a narrow rollout also narrows the fix. That is the operator's call, not mine.
- **Deployed ≠ observed.** Merging this proves nothing on the fleet. What would: a `coverage_side_ungradeable` count of **0** in steady state (a non-zero one means real positions are hitting the refusal and the venue read is not what we think), and — the actual criterion — a re-arm on a position whose side-blind coverage exceeded its size. Given `n = 1` and constructed, that may never be seen, and **not seeing it is not evidence the fix is wrong**.
- **Backlog row for `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json`** (I did not place it — the file is under a live drain):

> **`BL-20260902-BYBIT-REARM-GRADED-BOOK-DEPLOYED-NOT-OBSERVED`** — The Bybit naked sweep's re-arm decision now grades coverage of the book it is protecting (`bybit_leg_sides.graded_book_coverage`) instead of the side-blind `covered_qty`, closing the masking #10739 named: an other-book leg pushing the sum past `size` on a position whose own stop is gone, which `if covered + eps >= size: continue` skipped as fully covered. ⚠️ **n = 1, CONSTRUCTED from the live 2026-09-02T03:30:33Z `bybit_1`/BTCUSDT read — NO LIVE INSTANCE OF THE MASKING WAS EVER OBSERVED, and this row must not be read as recording one.** The fix is therefore **deployed and unobserved**; a green test suite is not the fleet. Two residuals, both out of this PR's scope: (a) the gate is **fleet-wide with no `*_ACCOUNTS` allowlist**, unlike every sibling order-path gate, so it cannot be staged on `bybit_1` before it binds on mainnet `bybit_2` — an operator decision, not a bug; (b) `scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py` keeps its **own** side-blind coverage arithmetic (`sl_covered_qty`/`uncovered_qty`), so the offline audit and the live sweep now answer the coverage question differently — a second derivation free to drift, which is the shape this repo keeps paying for. Watch `coverage_side_ungradeable` in the sweep summary: a persistently non-zero count means live positions are hitting the *we-could-not-look* refusal and the venue read is not what the split assumes.
